inlines.v: HER'ITABLE, adjective [from the root of heir, Latin haeres.] 1. Capable of inheriting, or taking by descent. By the canon law this son shall be legitimate and heritable 2. That may be inherited. [This is the true sense.] 3. Annexed to estates of inheritance. In Scot's law, heritable rights are all rights that affect lands or other immovables.
